generated.what_happened: The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate surged 19 basis points to 7.49% for the week ended October 2, reaching its highest level in nearly three years alongside rising 10-year Treasury yields and inflation. This increase further strained housing affordability, causing overall mortgage application volumes to fall 4.2% week-on-week as refinancing applications dropped 8% and purchase applications declined 2%. In response to the rising borrowing costs, President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve board members and argued that interest rates should decrease, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent attributed the high rates to a temporary energy shock stemming from the conflict with Iran.
